claims.text: 2026 general (unofficial, all 424 precincts reporting): Tran 151,971 (61.0%), Vo 97,070 (39.0%).
Subcommittees: Readiness; Intelligence and Special Operations; Oversight, Investigations and Regulations (Ranking Member); Contracting and Infrastructure.
Co-founder of the Lowering Costs Caucus.
Member of the New Democrat Coalition.
Co-chair of the Democratic Caucus National Security Task Force.
One of five Democrats who formally nominated Jeffries for Speaker in the caucus vote on Nov 18, 2026.
Hosted Jeffries in the district for a roundtable with veterans and local leaders (Mar 2026).
Pointed to Jeffries' proposal on Israel aid in his statement backing the Massie amendment (Jul 2026).
Issued a statement praising Jeffries' election as the Democratic nominee for Speaker (Nov 18, 2026).
2024: UDP's only California House spending was in CA-34 and CA-47. In CA-47 it spent over $4 million, mostly on TV and mailers, against Dave Min before the March primary. Min won anyway.
2026: FEC independent-expenditure records show no UDP spending for or against Tran. UDP's California money this cycle went to the CA-14 race.
In 2023–24, AIPAC's PAC gave $19,512 to his Republican opponent, Michelle Steel, and nothing to Tran (total of the itemized gifts dated 2023 and 2024).
Track AIPAC's figure for Tran counts money from pro-Israel donors and PACs; FEC records show most of it came through J Street. It is not UDP spending.
